This game uses generative AI in two ways.
During play: the character's replies are written by a language model and spoken by a speech model, and she can compose a short song when you ask for one. All of these models run on your own PC. The game does not connect to any outside AI service, and nothing you type or say is uploaded. Voices are synthetic; you can also create a voice from a recording you supply, which stays on your PC.
Made ahead of time: a library of body gestures the character uses while talking, the loading-screen illustration and some store artwork were made with generative models and reviewed by the developer. On the store page, the main trailer and the clips and images marked "AI-enhanced" are in-game footage re-rendered by video and image models to look more lifelike; some hairstyles and outfits in them are concept looks for future updates. Clips marked "In-game capture" and the trailer titled "Gameplay Trailer" are unprocessed. The trailers use AI-generated music.
Replies are generated live, so they can be wrong or out of character. You can report inappropriate AI output through the Steam Overlay.

Infinite GalGame is an AI-driven visual novel engine that generates a completely unique story every time you play.
﻿
There is no fixed script. No predetermined ending. You type — and the AI writes the next scene.
﻿
🎮 How It Works
﻿
Launch the game, click Start, and an opening scene is generated instantly. From there, choose from suggested options or type your own response freely. The AI director crafts each turn: dialogue, character emotion, scene atmosphere, and a matching anime-style CG illustration — all in real time.
﻿
✨ Features
﻿
∙ Truly Infinite Stories Every playthrough is different. The AI generates dialogue, plot twists, and character moments on the fly — no two sessions will ever be alike.
﻿
∙ Anime CG Illustration Each scene is paired with a freshly generated visual novel-style illustration. Characters maintain a consistent appearance throughout your story.
﻿
∙ Custom Character Cards Import SillyTavern-compatible character cards (PNG) to play with your own characters — complete with custom personality, backstory, scenario, and opening lines.
﻿
∙ Save & Load System Save your story progress at any point and pick up right where you left off.
﻿
∙ Bilingual Support Switch seamlessly between Chinese and English. Story content, UI, and AI output all adapt to your chosen language.
﻿
∙ Optional AI Voice Characters can speak their lines aloud with AI-generated voices matched to their gender, age, and personality.
﻿
∙ Safe & Moderated Built-in multi-layer content safety: keyword filtering on both input and output, AI self-review on every response, and a one-click in-game report system.
﻿
📝 Note Infinite GalGame requires an internet connection to generate stories. Content is produced by AI and may occasionally be imperfect — use the in-game report button to flag anything unusual.

We want to be fully transparent with our community about how we develop our game. In this project, we have integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools as an operational support for our team.
How we use it:
- Process optimization: It helps us streamline technical tasks and repetitive workflows.
- Efficiency: It allows us to deliver better work and move forward much faster.
- Resource maximization: It enables the team to save time on mechanical processes to focus on the final game polish.
Our commitment to craftsmanship:
- Total human control: No element of the final game has been left solely to AI.
- Expert review: Every technical asset or piece of content goes through a rigorous human editing filter.
- Manual work behind everything: Technology only optimizes our delivery times, but there is always genuine craftsmanship behind every asset.
- Guaranteed quality: We use AI to empower our team's capabilities, ensuring the essence and final finish of the game remain 100% human.
Thank you for your constant support!

AI-Generated Content Disclosure
I am a solo developer with no programming background. Before using AI, I spent three months following YouTube tutorials, deleted everything and restarted three times, and typed every line of code myself until the foundation of this game clicked.
From there, I used AI — primarily Claude — as a teacher and debugging partner across 7,000+ conversations over 16 months to learn GDScript and build every system in the game. The first line in my prompts is always "Stop being a yes sayer and always be brutal and honest."
Here is exactly what AI was and wasn't used for:
Code: I spent my first three months writing every line of code by hand. As the project grew, AI became a development partner — drafting code from my descriptions, which I then reviewed, debugged, and integrated. AI taught me programming concepts and helped me solve problems. Every design decision and system architecture is mine.
Art: AI-generated with extensive human direction and manual editing. Some pieces required 15 pages of descriptions. I often assemble final art from multiple elements — finding references, combining parts, and making hands-on edits until it matches my vision.
Animation: The first 14 enemies and 2 bosses were animated by me personally in DragonBones. For newer content, I'm exploring AI-generated animations and working to make them feel personal and consistent with the game's style — you can see examples with the later bosses. Some of these I'm still not satisfied with and will redo, which is just part of the process.
Music: I produced 350+ tracks using AI music tools and curated the best for the game. All creative direction — mood, style, placement — is mine.
Writing: All card text, lore, descriptions, and UI text are written by me. AI occasionally helps with polish.
Game Design: Every mechanic, card interaction, and balance decision comes from a lifetime of gaming — hundreds of board games, decades of Magic: The Gathering, a career at Blizzard Entertainment, and more consoles than most people can count. AI does not design games. That part is entirely human.
EDIT1: I felt the need to mention that I got diagnosed with ADHD last year, at the age of 47. The reason I could never learn coding in a traditional way is my attention span. If I am not interested it is super hard, and if I am interested it is super awesome. I get excited when I can talk and describe how I want my game to feel and function. The AI converts that to code, and together we've created a way for me to follow my dream and make a game that I want to play. I have thought to myself many times during development that I wish I knew how to make this myself, and I wish I was able to just learn and do things like most people. But here we are.

AI is used to generate the voices and advice of two opposing royal advisers (Left and Right Councillor). Each turn they comment on the situation and recommend different actions. If the player’s decree aligns more closely with one adviser’s stance, that adviser’s credibility increases while the other’s decreases.
As the credibility gap grows, public trust is affected, reflecting rising factional tension. If an adviser’s credibility reaches zero, they resign—sometimes angrily—warning the player not to dismiss their counsel. The vacant seat is then filled by a successor adviser, represented by a different local LLM model. This creates shifting personalities and advice styles across runs.
AI does not determine the game’s outcomes. Core consequences and metric changes are resolved by the game’s rule system; AI provides narrative and guidance within that system.
